newsitem.title: USA: Thermo Cardiosystems buys Thermo Electron unit.
newsitem.headline: Thermo Cardiosystems buys Thermo Electron unit.

text.p: Thermo Cardiosystems Inc.said Friday it has acquired International Technidyne Corp., a subsidiary of Thermo Electron Corp., in a stock deal valued at about $88.9 million.
Woburn, Mass.-based Thermo Cardiosystems, a researcher and manufacturer of implantable heart devices, offered 3,355,705 new shares of its stock for International Technidyne in a pooling of interests.
Thermo Cardiosystems' stock fell $1.125 to $26 on the American Stock Exchange in afternoon trading. Thermo Electron fell 37.5 cents to $34.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The issuance of the new Thermo Cardiosystems shares is subject to approval by the company's shareholders, it said.
Based in Edison, N.J., International Technidyne manufactures blood coagulation testing equipment, as well as skin incision devices. It earned $4.7 million on revenues of $34 million last year.
"This acquisition broadens our product base and provides another avenue for growth," said Thermo Cardiosystems Chief Executive Victor Poirier.

Separately, the company said its net income fell to $1.9 million, or 5 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 29, from $3.4 million, or 8 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues slid to $14.9 million from $15.4 million.
